claims.statement: Tsutomu Yamaguchi survived the Hiroshima bombing on August6,1945 and the Nagasaki bombing on August9,1945.
claims.locator: Testimony profile and printed107–109; AFP employment/second-blast paragraphs; Nagasaki Records overview
claims.qualification: Core chronology independently corroborated; survival does not mean unharmed or immune.

claims.statement: Yamaguchi worked in ship design for Mitsubishi and was in Hiroshima on a business assignment.
claims.qualification: Commercial ship-design role; not an invented military officer or nuclear scientist.

claims.statement: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on August6,1945; the detonation was at8:15am.
claims.locator: Hiroshima official section August6,1945–8:15am; Nagasaki Records overview
claims.qualification: Time is local; do not depict ground-level detonation or claim every death instantaneous.

claims.statement: Yamaguchi suffered severe burns in Hiroshima and survived.
claims.qualification: Left face/arm recollection; exact medical severity classification and distances omitted.

claims.statement: He boarded a train on August7 and returned to Nagasaki before the August9 bombing.
claims.locator: Testimony printed103–106; family printed22; AFP return paragraph
claims.qualification: Primary account specifies Koi departureAug7 and arrival late morningAug8. Family next-day return is compressed; script specifies boarding next day, not arriving then. Map links cities, not a verified railway itinerary.

claims.statement: Back at work in Nagasaki on August9, he recalled describing Hiroshima to his section manager when the second blast occurred.
claims.locator: Testimony printed107–108; AFP second-blast paragraph; family printed22
claims.qualification: Conversation is his retrospective recollection, not an independently recorded dialogue. No quotation or inner thought invented.

claims.statement: A US atomic bomb exploded over Nagasaki on August9,1945 at11:02am.
claims.qualification: The second attack was a separate bomb and city. No implication the first cloud physically followed him.

claims.statement: Yamaguchi, his wife and infant son survived the1945 bombings relevant to their exposure.
claims.qualification: Wife/son were Nagasaki survivors, not represented as accompanying him to Hiroshima. Infant age differs five/six months; script says infant.

claims.statement: The bombings killed tens of thousands of people and left lasting suffering.
claims.locator: Hiroshima damage and radiation sections; Nagasaki records; family testimony printed24–26
claims.qualification: Broad conservative statement; no immediate/late total conflation or medical cause assigned to an individual.

claims.statement: In March2009 Japanese authorities officially recognized Yamaguchi as exposed to both bombings.
claims.qualification: Nagasaki added Hiroshima exposure to his survivor record. This was not a new discovery that no one else survived twice.

claims.statement: Yamaguchi was not the only person to survive both atomic bombings.
claims.locator: Testimony printed109 names fellow double victims; AFP2006 documentary with seven others; family printed22
claims.qualification: No exact global number or currently only recognized status claimed.

claims.locator: AFP death opening, MondayJan4,2010; family profile printed21
claims.qualification: Stomach cancer reported by family; no assertion that either exposure caused his individual cancer.

claims.statement: In later life Yamaguchi publicly advocated nuclear abolition.
claims.locator: Testimony printed110 epilogue; family printed31–35; AFP Calls for peace
claims.qualification: Not a verbatim quotation or assertion of uninterrupted lifetime activism.

claims.statement: He recalled walking toward the Hiroshima shipyard from the Enami tram terminus when he saw the flash.
claims.qualification: Reserve: different secondary descriptions/distances; primary recollection only, no exact distance rendered.

claims.statement: His daughter reported persistent burn problems, hearing loss, cataracts and later illness; relatives also reported prolonged suffering.
claims.qualification: Reserve: family recollection, no inspected clinical records. Specific diagnosis/individual radiation-causation and heritable effects are not independently verified.

claims.statement: After the war he worked as an interpreter and teacher, then returned to Mitsubishi.
claims.locator: Testimony profile87 and printed108–109; contemporaneous obituary reporting inspected
claims.qualification: Reserve; return year1956 according to testimony. No need to compress this into narrated short.

excluded: Exact distance or verified railway itinerary
Specific radiation-cancer causation or inherited effects
Only began speaking publicly in2005 (family describes earlier interviews; later advocacy intensified)
